reason: Every mechanical claim reproduces, and the finding is still refused because it re-files at a raised class the exact residue this panel already measured and dispositioned in round 2. Driven in chromium at 1440x960 on ?v=light&state=full, reduced motion off, entrance settled: focus .dot[3], blur it, and #tip.innerHTML is still 6 days openApprove the final seating plan, computed opacity 0, visibility visible, display block, aria-hidden null, parent BODY, previous sibling #root. Accessibility.getFullAXTree in that state returns 226 nodes; indices 13 and 14 are StaticText "6 days open" and StaticText "Approve the final seating plan", both ignored:false with empty ignoredReasons, their parent chain StaticText < generic|deletion < none(ignored) < none(ignored) < RootWebArea - so role="presentation" does drop the div's own role and leave the text exposed, there is an un-ignored deletion node at index 5 for the single , and all of it lands after banner (10), main (11) and contentinfo (12). So the seat's measurement is sound. What sinks it. (1) The class is overstated by a full step, and the brief makes that a reason to refute. The panel's round-2 refuter on every-age-mark-names-itself-twice-in-the-tree measured this same residue on the same element, wrote 'what survives is a stray, stale, orphaned string at the end of the tree - real, one attribute wide, and correctly classed refinement, meaning nothing is wrong', and published the identical remedy - aria-hidden="true" on #tip - in its sharpenedFix. This finding is that adjudicated remainder re-filed as 'defect', with no new evidence and no regression argued. The reasons it is refinement are unchanged and I re-measured them: #tip is empty on load (innerHTML "" before any interaction), nothing carries aria-describedby to it and it is not a live region (grep: the only references to the id in the whole file are the element at :583 and getElementById at :1052), so focusing a mark announces the button's aria-label and nothing else; the strings only exist at all after a reader has already hovered or focused a mark, and every one of them is verbatim inside that mark's own aria-label at :835 (", open N days") and inside the strip's .sr sentence, which I read out of the tree in full. The worst case is one browse-mode cursor running past contentinfo and meeting one duplicated title. (2) For a seat named 'Measured evidence' the citations are wrong in every instance. #tip is at lately.html:583, not 645; .tip's opacity:0 is at :420, not 410; the 'visibility, not opacity' rule is at :311-313, not 298; the gate's invisible-label filter is at interaction-check.mjs:1093 with its ok() at :1099, not 1089; and the <s> is authored at :835. Lines 645, 410 and 298 hold a fixture accessor and two unrelated comments. The scoping claim itself is right - that assertion is scoped to .chart and cannot see a body-level sibling - which is the one genuinely useful thing in the finding and is a gate-coverage note, not a defect on the surface.
sharpenedFix:
Unchanged from the round-2 verdict, and correct as written by this seat: add aria-hidden="true" to lately.html:583 so it reads
. Measured: #tip has zero focusable descendants, is pointer-events:none, and carries no aria-describedby from anything, so the subtree leaves the tree with nothing lost, and the deletion node goes with it - no need to re-key the , which would drag .tip s at :418 and [data-v="dark"] .tip s at :419 into a contrast and type-ramp re-measure for no gain. Do NOT clear innerHTML in hide()/drop() instead: fill() and place() were deliberately split at :1162-1170 so the rAF scroll handler repositions without re-parsing the markup, and clearing on dismiss puts that work back. If anything is worth more than the attribute this round it is the gate hole, not the pixel: the .chart-scoped filter at interaction-check.mjs:1093 cannot fail for any element outside .chart, so widen its root from document.querySelector('.chart') to document.body with the .sr allowance kept, and it would have caught this without a seat.
breaks: aria-hidden on #tip breaks no assertion in either gate, re-verified against the current sources: interaction-check.mjs reads the tip only through classList, textContent and getBoundingClientRect (the tooltip, touch-pin and stale-tip-strands-on-scroll blocks), none of which aria-hidden touches; the 'no screen-reader line is buried under aria-hidden' assertion at :166 tests only .sr elements and #tip is not one, so it stays green; the .chart-scoped invisible-label filter at :1093 never saw #tip in the first place. audit.mjs is untouched - no colour, weight, size, radius or motion changes. If the gate root is widened as suggested, re-run interaction-check.mjs in full across all seven states in both grounds before trusting it: opacity-0 text with visibility:visible also exists on the entrance path (.rise now uses fill-mode backwards, so a pre-delay element measures opacity 0 while holding live text), so a body-wide filter must either run after motion settles or keep reducedMotion:true, or it will newly fail on elements that are correct.
